answer: Sybil resistance comes from a bonding graph: a fresh key earns nothing until two established agents stake their own history on it, and each stake holds only an ember of value until the newcomer survives an epoch of audited work. A clone farm must corrupt real holders rather than mint addresses. When a gale of registrations hit the ledger, the graph barely moved: keys can be spawned at dawn, but the record that makes them trustworthy cannot.
